name: ClickHouse
look: Near-black canvas with electric yellow on CTAs and huge stat numbers, dark cards barely lighter than the ground.

hero.title: The fastest analytical database
hero.sub: Columnar storage, vectorised execution and aggressive compression. Billions of rows scanned per second on hardware you already have.

features.title: Columnar, vectorised, compressed
features.sub: Three decisions made at the storage layer that no amount of query tuning elsewhere can match.

items.title: Columnar storage
items.body: Only the columns a query touches are read from disk, which for wide analytical tables is most of the win.

items.title: Vectorised execution
items.body: Operations run over blocks of thousands of values, keeping the CPU pipeline full.

items.title: 10× compression
items.body: Sorted columnar data compresses hard. Typical deployments store a tenth of the raw bytes.

items.title: Scales horizontally
items.body: Shard and replicate across nodes, with distributed queries planned automatically.

items.title: Speaks SQL
items.body: Ordinary SQL with analytical extensions. Your BI tool connects over the existing wire protocols.

items.title: Cloud or self-hosted
items.body: The same engine, managed by us or running on your own tin. Open source either way.

showcases.title: Reproducible, not marketing
showcases.body: Every published benchmark ships with the dataset, the queries and the hardware specification. A result you cannot reproduce is a result we should not have published.

showcases.title: Managed, without the lock-in
showcases.body: The managed service runs the same open-source engine. Export your data as Parquet at any time and stand it up yourself — the migration path out is documented, not hypothetical.

gallery.title: Documentation
gallery.sub: Getting started, SQL reference, deployment and tuning.

testimonial.quote: A dashboard that took ninety seconds now takes under one. We did not rewrite the queries — we moved the table.
testimonial.name: Priya Venkatesh

pricing.title: Pricing
pricing.sub: Open source is free. Cloud is priced on compute and storage.

items.a: No. The managed service runs the same Apache 2.0 engine with no proprietary query features. You are paying for operations, not capability.

items.q: Can it replace my transactional database?
items.a: No, and it should not try. It is built for analytical scans over large tables, not high-concurrency single-row writes.

items.q: How does it compress so well?
items.a: Columnar layout plus sorting means adjacent values are similar, which general-purpose compressors exploit heavily. Ten-to-one is typical on real data.
Export to Parquet and stand up your own cluster. The path is documented and customers do take it — that is the point of keeping the engine open.

cta.title: Query a billion rows
cta.sub: Free to start, and the open-source engine is the same one.

notes: Near-pure black with white type. There is no light-mode marketing surface in this system.
Electric yellow carries primary CTAs, the large stat-callout numbers, and full-bleed yellow bands — nothing else.
Cards sit barely lighter than the canvas. The colour-block contrast is deliberately subtle.
Huge yellow stat numbers in a heavy sans carry the credibility moment. That is the pattern, not a decorative flourish.
Radius is hierarchical: 8px buttons, 12px content cards, and pills only on tag badges.
